title: Hydrocele surgery
what: The surgeon removes the extra fluid around the testicle and treats the lining so fluid does not build up again.
why: When the scrotum is enlarged by fluid, bothers you, or hurts. In young children, a hydrocele often goes away on its own. The doctor will decide if surgery is needed.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; you usually go home the same day or after 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to do
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
For a child: past illnesses and vaccinations

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests and a scrotal ultrasound. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthesia
prepare.text: Adults may have local, spinal, or general anesthesia. Children usually have general anesthesia. An anesthetist will talk with you.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food or drink for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
The surgeon makes a small cut in the scrotum, or in the groin for children
The fluid is removed, and the lining is treated
Sometimes a small drain tube is placed
feel: Pain at the stitches. You will get painkillers
Swelling of the scrotum for a few days or weeks
after: Wear snug underwear, and use cold as your doctor advises
No heavy lifting or sports for a few weeks
A follow-up visit when your doctor says
red_flags: The scrotum suddenly gets bigger and very painful
Pus or redness at the stitches

faq.q: Will a hydrocele go away on its own?
faq.a: In babies up to 1 to 2 years old, it often does. In adults, it usually does not go away without treatment.
Usually not. The testicle is not removed.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your documents, test results, and snug underwear. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
